word_order: SVO — verbs precede objects in many examples (e.g. "made them stand out", "are advised to be aware").
punctuation_present: always — as observed in the sample
register: edited written prose (encyclopedic / news / travel advice) — formal, informational sentences.
notes_for_prompt_writer: Prefer to emit segments at strong sentence delimiters (sentence-final punctuation, semicolons, and colons introducing independent clauses). Treat commas as potential but weak boundaries: only split at commas when followed by coordinating conjunctions (", and", ", but", ", or", ", so") or clearly independent clauses. Never start a new segment with closing punctuation or a closing bracket/quote; attach them to the preceding unit. Special-case common abbreviations and numeric punctuation (Dr., U.S., 1,000, 3.14) to avoid false sentence breaks, and avoid splitting immediately after subordinating conjunctions or short prepositions (unstable prefixes).
